title: Certificate in Applied Generative & Agentic AI
summary: Build practical LLM applications using prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, and tool-using agents.
capstone: RAG-powered domain assistant evolved into a single tool-using agent with an evaluation report.
delivery: Self-paced draft modules with proposed weekend workshops, peer discussion and office hours; no cohort scheduled.
outcomes: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for an internal knowledge desk.
O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for an internal knowledge desk.
O3: Evaluate ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases against a baseline.
O4: Demonstrate privacy minimization, human approval and recoverable failure.
O5: Defend a retrieval-assistant development portfolio with reproducible evidence and limitations.

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

activity.title: Define the decision boundary — applied workshop
activity.objective: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for an internal knowledge desk.
activity.overview: You support an internal knowledge desk. Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

steps.title: Research and discussion · 15 minutes
steps.text: Compare with a peer, cite your reading and identify a failure condition.

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes
steps.text: Explain why a simulation is not a production-ready system; name the accountable owner.

reflection: What evidence changes your decision?
Which error is more costly here?
What information can you avoid retaining?

title: Professional Certificate in Agentic AI Systems
summary: Design and deploy production multi-agent systems with orchestration, memory, tool protocols, evaluation, observability, deployment, and security.
capstone: Production multi-agent system with tool protocol integration, evaluation suite, tracing, guardrails, and deployment runbook.
format: 18 weeks, online; weekly mentored sessions plus a monthly live faculty masterclass

credential.rule: Every approved required course at C or better. Required-course list and final grading policy TBC.
credential.sourceDraftRules: Historical source additionally proposes 70% overall, all labs, capstone pass, and 80% participation/approved alternative. These are draft proposals, not activated issuance rules.

support: Scholarion AI Teaching Assistant (coaches; never completes graded work)
structure: Block B (Weeks 10–18): Production multi-agent systems; final exam replaced by capstone defense
weeks: 0 (optional)
Python and tooling refresher: VS Code, Colab, Git, virtual environments, API basics
Agentic systems: autonomy levels, agent loops, and when not to use agents
LLM foundations for builders: tokens, context, sampling, structured output, cost and latency
Instruction design for agents: system prompts and output schemas
Tool use and function calling: error handling and idempotent tools
Retrieval systems: embeddings, chunking, vector stores, hybrid search and reranking
Agentic RAG: routing, query planning, self-correction and citation grounding
Planning and reasoning patterns: reason-act loops, plan-and-execute and reflection
Memory and context management: short/long-term memory, summarization and context budgets
Midterm project plus Block A exam
Small language models for agents: local inference and SLM/LLM routing
Multi-agent architectures: orchestrator–worker, hierarchical, critic/reviewer and handoffs
Frameworks lab: graph-based orchestration and role-based crews; versions verified at build time
Tool and context protocols such as MCP: secure servers and clients
Agentic coding: repository tasks, test-first workflows and review gates
Evaluation: task success, trajectory evaluation, calibrated LLM-as-judge and regression suites
Observability, security and guardrails: tracing, injection defense, permissions, sandboxing and human oversight
Deployment: APIs, containers, cost controls, monitoring and rollback
Capstone defense and demo day

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

activity.title: Define the decision boundary — applied workshop
activity.objective: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a multi-agent service desk.
activity.overview: You support a multi-agent service desk. Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

steps.title: Research and discussion · 15 minutes
steps.text: Compare with a peer, cite your reading and identify a failure condition.

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes
steps.text: Explain why a simulation is not a production-ready system; name the accountable owner.

reflection: What evidence changes your decision?
Which error is more costly here?
What information can you avoid retaining?

capstonePackage.exemplar: A fictional approval queue retains missing scores, routes uncertainty to review and never executes updates. Its evidence pack records input versions, thresholds, subgroup counts, failed cases and a rollback owner. Adapt this scaffold to the program brief. This is not a finished capstone solution.
capstonePackage.peerReview: A peer challenges an unsupported claim and repeats one test; the author documents the response.
capstonePackage.status: Draft brief; finished program-specific exemplars require SME authoring.

evaluationPlan.pre: Explain a bounded workflow before instruction and attempt the first practice pool.

title: AI-Native Professional: Workflows & Agents for Everyday Productivity
summary: Use AI assistants, reusable prompt systems, and lightweight agents to improve everyday professional workflows.
capstone: Personal productivity agent stack with documented time-savings measurement.
prerequisites: Basic digital literacy; no coding required
delivery: Self-paced draft modules with proposed weekend workshops, peer discussion and office hours; no cohort scheduled.
outcomes: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a personal task workspace.
O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for a personal task workspace.
O3: Evaluate ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases against a baseline.
O4: Demonstrate privacy minimization, human approval and recoverable failure.

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

activity.title: Define the decision boundary — applied workshop

activity.overview: You support a personal task workspace. Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints.

title: Certificate in No-Code Generative AI & Agent Workflows
summary: Create prompting workflows, knowledge assistants, no-code RAG solutions, and automated agent workflows.
capstone: No-code knowledge assistant and automated workflow for a department process.
prerequisites: Basic digital literacy; no coding required
delivery: Self-paced draft modules with proposed weekend workshops, peer discussion and office hours; no cohort scheduled.
outcomes: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a departmental request desk.
O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for a departmental request desk.
O3: Evaluate ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases against a baseline.
O4: Demonstrate privacy minimization, human approval and recoverable failure.
O5: Defend a no-code knowledge workflows portfolio with reproducible evidence and limitations.

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

activity.title: Define the decision boundary — applied workshop
activity.objective: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a departmental request desk.
activity.overview: You support a departmental request desk. Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

steps.title: Research and discussion · 15 minutes
steps.text: Compare with a peer, cite your reading and identify a failure condition.

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes
steps.text: Explain why a simulation is not a production-ready system; name the accountable owner.

reflection: What evidence changes your decision?
Which error is more costly here?
What information can you avoid retaining?

capstonePackage.exemplar: A fictional approval queue retains missing scores, routes uncertainty to review and never executes updates. Its evidence pack records input versions, thresholds, subgroup counts, failed cases and a rollback owner. Adapt this scaffold to the program brief. This is not a finished capstone solution.
capstonePackage.peerReview: A peer challenges an unsupported claim and repeats one test; the author documents the response.
capstonePackage.status: Draft brief; finished program-specific exemplars require SME authoring.

evaluationPlan.pre: Explain a bounded workflow before instruction and attempt the first practice pool.
evaluationPlan.post: Use unseen synthetic cases and compare outcome-aligned rubric scores.
evaluationPlan.analytics: Local practice attempts and module checkpoints, not official grades.

transferPolicy: No automatic credit. Map outcomes and assessed evidence; an educator approves equivalence and prevents duplicate credit. Dependencies #1–#14 remain TBC.

title: Certificate in AI Agents for Business Operations
summary: Implement AI agents in business processes such as customer service triage, procurement, operations, and workflow coordination.
capstone: Business-process agent with an ROI case and governance plan.
delivery: Self-paced draft modules with proposed weekend workshops, peer discussion and office hours; no cohort scheduled.
outcomes: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a procurement intake process.
O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for a procurement intake process.
O3: Evaluate ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases against a baseline.
O4: Demonstrate privacy minimization, human approval and recoverable failure.
O5: Defend a operations improvement portfolio with reproducible evidence and limitations.

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

activity.title: Define the decision boundary — applied workshop
activity.objective: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a procurement intake process.
activity.overview: You support a procurement intake process. Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

steps.title: Research and discussion · 15 minutes
steps.text: Compare with a peer, cite your reading and identify a failure condition.

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes
steps.text: Explain why a simulation is not a production-ready system; name the accountable owner.

reflection: What evidence changes your decision?
Which error is more costly here?
What information can you avoid retaining?
activity.submission: Draft cohort policy: 2–3-page APA-style paper with relevant code, output screenshots and citations. Word/PDF upload and Sunday 11:59 PM deadline need a scheduled cohort; no live deadline is set.
activity.integrity: AI coaching on concepts and ungraded practice is allowed with disclosure. Graded reasoning must be your own.

miniLabs.title: Scale and subgroup check
miniLabs.task: Use the 60-row assignment dataset; compare queues and state a sampling limitation.

quiz.prompt: Which boundary is testable?
choices: A named task with allowed actions and a human escalation owner
A promise to automate the department
Skip review and trust the output.
quiz.explanation: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

quiz.prompt: Your team supporting a procurement intake process cannot reproduce a result. What next?
choices: Publish because the report looks complete.
Reproduce the inputs, versions and checks before accepting the claim.
Remove failing examples.
quiz.explanation: Keep failures visible. A claim needs reproducible evidence.

quiz.prompt: Which artifact best demonstrates define the decision boundary?
choices: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Include results and limitations.
A screenshot with no inputs or explanation.
An assertion of perfect accuracy.
quiz.explanation: A concrete artifact and observed evidence support review.

masteryPath.remediation: Re-read the concept, repeat the missing-input task and explain the mistake before retrying.
masteryPath.enrichment: Change an assumption, create a counterexample and compare error rates.

activity.overview: You support a procurement intake process. Reproduce one success and one failure; defend the boundary.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: Connect claims to reproducible evidence and explain failures. Present baseline, design, controls and rollback. A polished success-only demonstration is not enough.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Calculate reviewed count, total and review rate for each fictional queue; missing confidence requires review. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Reproduce one success and one failure; defend the boundary. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

steps.title: Research and discussion · 15 minutes
steps.text: Compare with a peer, cite your reading and identify a failure condition.

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes
steps.text: Explain why a simulation is not a production-ready system; name the accountable owner.

reflection: What evidence changes your decision?
Which error is more costly here?
What information can you avoid retaining?
activity.submission: Draft cohort policy: 2–3-page APA-style paper with relevant code, output screenshots and citations. Word/PDF upload and Sunday 11:59 PM deadline need a scheduled cohort; no live deadline is set.
activity.integrity: AI coaching on concepts and ungraded practice is allowed with disclosure. Graded reasoning must be your own.

modules.labTask: Calculate reviewed count, total and review rate for each fictional queue; missing confidence requires review.

miniLabs.title: Missing-input stress test
miniLabs.task: Replace every fourth confidence with None. Re-run and explain the changed results.

miniLabs.title: Scale and subgroup check
miniLabs.task: Use the 60-row assignment dataset; compare queues and state a sampling limitation.

quiz.prompt: What is strongest evidence?
choices: Reproducible tests and candid failure analysis
A success-only recording
Skip review and trust the output.
quiz.explanation: Connect claims to reproducible evidence and explain failures. Present baseline, design, controls and rollback. A polished success-only demonstration is not enough.

quiz.prompt: Your team supporting a procurement intake process cannot reproduce a result. What next?
choices: Publish because the report looks complete.
Reproduce the inputs, versions and checks before accepting the claim.
Remove failing examples.
quiz.explanation: Keep failures visible. A claim needs reproducible evidence.

quiz.prompt: Which artifact best demonstrates capstone evaluation clinic?
choices: Reproduce one success and one failure; defend the boundary. Include results and limitations.
A screenshot with no inputs or explanation.
An assertion of perfect accuracy.
quiz.explanation: A concrete artifact and observed evidence support review.

modules.liveSession: Compare two approaches to capstone evaluation clinic and defend the review boundary.
modules.announcement: Module 12: Capstone evaluation clinic. Review the objective, run practice cases and bring a failure to discussion. Cohort dates pending.

masteryPath.remediation: Re-read the concept, repeat the missing-input task and explain the mistake before retrying.
masteryPath.enrichment: Change an assumption, create a counterexample and compare error rates.

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.text: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes

capstonePackage.exemplar: A fictional approval queue retains missing scores, routes uncertainty to review and never executes updates. Its evidence pack records input versions, thresholds, subgroup counts, failed cases and a rollback owner. Adapt this scaffold to the program brief. This is not a finished capstone solution.
capstonePackage.peerReview: A peer challenges an unsupported claim and repeats one test; the author documents the response.
capstonePackage.status: Draft brief; finished program-specific exemplars require SME authoring.

evaluationPlan.pre: Explain a bounded workflow before instruction and attempt the first practice pool.
evaluationPlan.post: Use unseen synthetic cases and compare outcome-aligned rubric scores.
evaluationPlan.analytics: Local practice attempts and module checkpoints, not official grades.

transferPolicy: No automatic credit. Map outcomes and assessed evidence; an educator approves equivalence and prevents duplicate credit. Dependencies #1–#14 remain TBC.

title: Professional Certificate in Applied AI: Machine Learning, Generative AI & Agents
summary: Move from classical ML and deep learning into generative AI and agentic workflows in one integrated pathway.
capstone: End-to-end project combining an ML model, a GenAI feature, and an agentic workflow on one dataset.
delivery: Self-paced draft modules with proposed weekend workshops, peer discussion and office hours; no cohort scheduled.
outcomes: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for an operations analysis team.
O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for an operations analysis team.
O3: Evaluate ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases against a baseline.
O4: Demonstrate privacy minimization, human approval and recoverable failure.
O5: Defend a applied AI analysis portfolio with reproducible evidence and limitations.

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

activity.title: Define the decision boundary — applied workshop
activity.objective: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for an operations analysis team.
activity.overview: You support an operations analysis team. Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

steps.title: Research and discussion · 15 minutes
steps.text: Compare with a peer, cite your reading and identify a failure condition.

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes
steps.text: Explain why a simulation is not a production-ready system; name the accountable owner.

reflection: What evidence changes your decision?
Which error is more costly here?
What information can you avoid retaining?
activity.submission: Draft cohort policy: 2–3-page APA-style paper with relevant code, output screenshots and citations. Word/PDF upload and Sunday 11:59 PM deadline need a scheduled cohort; no live deadline is set.
activity.integrity: AI coaching on concepts and ungraded practice is allowed with disclosure. Graded reasoning must be your own.

modules.labTask: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action.

miniLabs.title: Missing-input stress test
miniLabs.task: Replace every fourth confidence with None. Re-run and explain the changed results.

miniLabs.title: Scale and subgroup check
miniLabs.task: Use the 60-row assignment dataset; compare queues and state a sampling limitation.

quiz.prompt: Which boundary is testable?
choices: A named task with allowed actions and a human escalation owner
A promise to automate the department
Skip review and trust the output.
quiz.explanation: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

quiz.prompt: Your team supporting an operations analysis team cannot reproduce a result. What next?
choices: Publish because the report looks complete.
Reproduce the inputs, versions and checks before accepting the claim.
Remove failing examples.
quiz.explanation: Keep failures visible. A claim needs reproducible evidence.

quiz.prompt: Which artifact best demonstrates define the decision boundary?
choices: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Include results and limitations.
A screenshot with no inputs or explanation.
An assertion of perfect accuracy.
quiz.explanation: A concrete artifact and observed evidence support review.

modules.liveSession: Compare two approaches to define the decision boundary and defend the review boundary.
modules.announcement: Module 1: Define the decision boundary. Review the objective, run practice cases and bring a failure to discussion. Cohort dates pending.

masteryPath.remediation: Re-read the concept, repeat the missing-input task and explain the mistake before retrying.
masteryPath.enrichment: Change an assumption, create a counterexample and compare error rates.

modules.title: Inspect data quality
modules.lesson: Missing values and duplicates change metric denominators. Separate schema checks from business rules; reject malformed records visibly rather than silently converting them to ordinary inputs.

activity.title: Inspect data quality — applied workshop
activity.objective: O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for an operations analysis team.
activity.overview: You support an operations analysis team. Count invalid and missing values before selecting records for analysis.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: Missing values and duplicates change metric denominators. Separate schema checks from business rules; reject malformed records visibly rather than silently converting them to ordinary inputs.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Keep rows with a numeric confidence between zero and one. Missing rows must not enter the accepted set. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Count invalid and missing values before selecting records for analysis. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

title: Certificate in AI Agents for Software Engineering
summary: Apply AI coding assistants and agents across planning, coding, testing, review, CI/CD, and secure repository workflows.
capstone: Agentic coding pipeline from issue to plan, code, tests, review, and security/quality gates.
prerequisites: Python, Git concepts and automated testing
delivery: Self-paced draft modules with proposed weekend workshops, peer discussion and office hours; no cohort scheduled.
outcomes: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a software delivery team.
O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for a software delivery team.
O3: Evaluate ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases against a baseline.
O4: Demonstrate privacy minimization, human approval and recoverable failure.
O5: Defend a software quality automation portfolio with reproducible evidence and limitations.

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

activity.title: Define the decision boundary — applied workshop
activity.objective: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a software delivery team.
activity.overview: You support a software delivery team. Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

steps.title: Research and discussion · 15 minutes
steps.text: Compare with a peer, cite your reading and identify a failure condition.

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes
steps.text: Explain why a simulation is not a production-ready system; name the accountable owner.

reflection: What evidence changes your decision?
Which error is more costly here?
What information can you avoid retaining?

title: Certificate in AI & Agentic AI for Healthcare Operations
summary: Use AI for healthcare operations such as scheduling, claims-documentation support, supply chain, and population-level analytics with strong governance.
capstone: Healthcare operations agent on synthetic data with privacy controls and a governance review.
delivery: Self-paced draft modules with proposed weekend workshops, peer discussion and office hours; no cohort scheduled.
outcomes: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a synthetic scheduling office.
O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for a synthetic scheduling office.
O3: Evaluate ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases against a baseline.
O4: Demonstrate privacy minimization, human approval and recoverable failure.
O5: Defend a non-clinical operations support portfolio with reproducible evidence and limitations.

modules.title: Define the decision boundary
modules.lesson: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

activity.title: Define the decision boundary — applied workshop
activity.objective: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a synthetic scheduling office.
activity.overview: You support a synthetic scheduling office. Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints.

steps.title: Concept setup · 10 minutes
steps.text: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

steps.title: Implementation · 20 minutes
steps.text: Map each ID to review if confidence is missing or below 0.8, otherwise ready_for_review. Neither route executes an action. Open the starter notebook or visual workflow simulator.

steps.title: Task · 20 minutes
steps.text: Draw an input-to-review map with two mandatory human checkpoints. Record a normal, missing-input and human-review case.

steps.title: Research and discussion · 15 minutes
steps.text: Compare with a peer, cite your reading and identify a failure condition.

steps.title: Wrap-up · 5 minutes
steps.text: Explain why a simulation is not a production-ready system; name the accountable owner.

reflection: What evidence changes your decision?
Which error is more costly here?
What information can you avoid retaining?
activity.submission: Draft cohort policy: 2–3-page APA-style paper with relevant code, output screenshots and citations. Word/PDF upload and Sunday 11:59 PM deadline need a scheduled cohort; no live deadline is set.
activity.integrity: AI coaching on concepts and ungraded practice is allowed with disclosure. Graded reasoning must be your own.

miniLabs.task: Replace every fourth confidence with None. Re-run and explain the changed results.

miniLabs.title: Scale and subgroup check

choices: A named task with allowed actions and a human escalation owner
A promise to automate the department
Skip review and trust the output.
quiz.explanation: An assistant can suggest an action without permission to perform it. Name the decision owner, allowed inputs, prohibited outputs and measurable baseline before selecting a model.

quiz.prompt: Your team supporting a synthetic scheduling office cannot reproduce a result. What next?
choices: Publish because the report looks complete.
Reproduce the inputs, versions and checks before accepting the claim.
Remove failing examples.
quiz.explanation: Keep failures visible. A claim needs reproducible evidence.

capstonePackage.exemplar: A fictional approval queue retains missing scores, routes uncertainty to review and never executes updates. Its evidence pack records input versions, thresholds, subgroup counts, failed cases and a rollback owner. Adapt this scaffold to the program brief. This is not a finished capstone solution.
capstonePackage.peerReview: A peer challenges an unsupported claim and repeats one test; the author documents the response.
capstonePackage.status: Draft brief; finished program-specific exemplars require SME authoring.

evaluationPlan.pre: Explain a bounded workflow before instruction and attempt the first practice pool.
evaluationPlan.post: Use unseen synthetic cases and compare outcome-aligned rubric scores.
evaluationPlan.analytics: Local practice attempts and module checkpoints, not official grades.

transferPolicy: No automatic credit. Map outcomes and assessed evidence; an educator approves equivalence and prevents duplicate credit. Dependencies #1–#14 remain TBC.
